MEASURED: Before the fix, growing Subject.closure from empty to 8,192 entries left retained_bytes at 318 while the closure payload is 65,536 bytes; four of the six new regression tests fail (repro-before-fix.txt).
After the fix the same graph charges 65,854 bytes, and a graph_bytes budget of 318 refuses it with E-BUDGET-GRAPH-BYTES (closure_storage_is_charged_and_budgeted).
Shape storage is charged: a 64-scalar right-nested ShapeTree adds 2,016 bytes of boxed pair allocations, and a budget covering only the flat estimate refuses the graph.
Fact payloads (one-hot groups, derived rule strings, evidence buffers) and node operation payloads (affine terms, index tables) raise the charge.
cargo test -p noble-ngraph passes in full; clippy with -D warnings is clean; rustfmt reports no diff (test-log.txt, clippy-log.txt, fmt-log.txt).
INFERRED: Hosts that retain graphs under a lowered graph_bytes quota now charge graph-owned metadata that was previously invisible; default-budget admission of ordinary graphs is unchanged because the added charge is far below 32 MiB.

not_proven: No process-memory measurement, allocator-overhead, or denial-of-service claim.
The u64 saturation path is unreachable in a test (it needs capacities near 2^61) and rests on saturating arithmetic plus review.
No claim about separately owned checker caches, which stay outside the documented contract.
